_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Follows on from EU/CatalogueOfESSStandards_scoping_2026-08-08.md (block E), which scoped the 12-member Catalogue of ESS Standards but minted nothing. This session researched 4 of the 8 unresearched candidate members directly at source (EBS business-registers manual, seasonal adjustment guidelines, temporal disaggregation guidelines, precision/variance handbook), confirmed SDMX's version history per Thomas's ruling (one node, versioned, not two), and left the remaining three exactly where the scoping doc's own rule says they belong: data validation 2.0 (source unreachable this session), GSBPM and ISCED (classification hubs -- per the scoping doc's own instruction, 'do not research it by reading it', edges come from citing programmes). Sitting in EU/proposals/ per that folder's rule.
_note: Domain tag on all six nodes below is 'national-accounts', matching the existing convention in ess-quality-framework.json -- every node in that sibling file uses the same tag regardless of its specific topic (SIMS, the SDMX glossary, the QPI guidelines are all tagged 'national-accounts' too). A loose fit but a consistent one; not treated as a new decision the way eu-budget was in the legal-instrument-lineages file, because this is following an existing precedent rather than inventing one.

reports.title: European business statistics methodological manual for statistical business registers
reports.description: Catalogue of ESS Standards member #3 (of 8 unresearched, per the scoping doc's ordering). 2021 edition confirmed by direct PDF fetch and extraction (Cat. No KS-GQ-20-006-EN-N, ISBN 978-92-76-20739-9, doi:10.2785/093371, 'Manuscript completed in January 2021'). Its own text: 'The updated manual has only 10 chapters compared with 24 chapters in the 2010 edition' -- confirming a genuine prior edition, not asserted from the scoping doc's speculation.
reports.cadence_note: 2010 edition -> 2021 edition, 11-year observed interval (Research.1.md section 4's 'latest observed interval' rule for irregular publications). Both editions confirmed at source this session.

release_schedule.note: This is a Eurostat methodological manual (not a periodic statistical release). Editions were published in 2010 and 2021 (2021 edition, product code KS-GQ-20-006, dated 16 Feb 2021), an 11-year gap. The 2021 foreword states the manual 'will be updated continuously on the statistical business register manual wiki and additional media if needed' rather than on a fixed edition cycle, so there is no stated rule or calendar for a next edition -- genuinely irregular/continuous revision.

reports.title: ESS Guidelines on Seasonal Adjustment
reports.description: Catalogue member #4. Three editions confirmed by direct fetch this session, not two as the scoping doc could only speculate: 2009 (KS-RA-09-006, found this session -- the scoping doc flagged a 2009 first edition as 'plausible... but not verified, do not assert it'; now verified), 2015 (KS-GQ-15-001, ISBN 978-92-79-45176-8, doi:10.2785/317290), and 2024 (KS-GQ-24-012, ISBN 978-92-68-15943-9, doi:10.2785/705102). The 2024 edition's own text: 'Following the 2009 and 2015 editions which were widely accepted and implemented, the 2024 revised ESS Guidelines on Seasonal Adjustment present theoretical aspects and practical implementation issues...'
reports.cadence_note: Latest observed interval: 2015 -> 2024 edition, 9 years. Matches the scoping doc's estimate, now confirmed against the actual 2024 document rather than inferred.

release_schedule.note: Guidelines have appeared three times: first edition 2009, revised version endorsed November 2014 (published 2015), and third edition 2024. Intervals were roughly 6 years then 9 years, with no stated periodicity or announced next-edition date. Eurostat's landing page for the 2024 edition and the document's own foreword give no planned update schedule, only noting that domain-specific seasonal adjustment policies are reviewed 'from year to year' operationally, which is a different, non-guideline-revision process.

reports.title: ESS guidelines on temporal disaggregation, benchmarking and reconciliation
reports.publisher: Eurostat, joint work with Istat, CBS, ONS, Statistics Denmark, Statistics Austria, Destatis and the Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
reports.description: Catalogue member #5. 2018 edition confirmed by direct PDF fetch (KS-06-18-355-EN-N, ISBN 978-92-79-98007-7, doi:10.2785/846595, 'Manuscript completed in November 2018'). Only one edition found this session -- cadence is genuinely open, not just unresearched, matching the scoping doc's own framing for this item.
reports.cadence_note: Only one edition identified (2018). Per Research.1.md section 4, cadence is preferred not required -- left absent rather than guessed. A 2024 CROS page on 'annual quarterly monthly data introduction, temporal disaggregation and benchmarking' turned up in the same search and may or may not be a successor edition of this document or a separate teaching resource; not opened this session, flagged in _open_questions.

reports.title: Handbook on precision requirements and variance estimation for ESS households surveys
reports.description: Catalogue member #6. 2013 edition confirmed by direct PDF fetch (KS-RA-13-029-EN, ISBN 978-92-79-31197-0, doi:10.2785/13579). Only one edition found -- same open-cadence situation as ess-temporal-disaggregation-guidelines.
reports.cadence_note: Only one edition identified (2013). Six-year gap between issue (2013) and the catalogue's own recorded ESSC approval (February 2017) per the scoping doc -- an approval-lag, not a second edition; do not mistake it for cadence evidence.

reports.title: SDMX (Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange)
reports.publisher: SDMX Technical Working Group (central banks, statistical offices and international organisations, including Eurostat, ECB, IMF, UN, OECD, BIS and the World Bank)
reports.description: Catalogue members #10 and #11, minted as ONE node per Thomas's ruling 2026-08-09: 'treat SDMX as a single evolving standard with version history in its description, not two separate nodes' -- the opposite of how the source catalogue itself lists 2.0 and 2.1 as separate entries. Version history confirmed by direct fetch of sdmx.org/standards-2/: 1.0, 2.0 (catalogue: dateAccepted 02/2007, issued 2005), 2.1 (catalogue: dateAccepted 02/2007, issued 2012; 2.1 itself saw further amendments in 2011, 2012, 2013 and a major consolidation in July 2020 adopting VTL 2.0), 3.0 (September 2021), 3.1 (May 2025). SDMX 3.0 and 3.1 are NOT in the ESS Catalogue (per the scoping doc) but are included in this node's version history since Thomas's ruling treats SDMX as one continuously-evolving standard rather than a fixed catalogue snapshot. Distinct from the corpus's existing sdmx-glossary node (ess-quality-framework.json), which is a different, separate document.
reports.cadence_note: Irregular major-version releases (2.0, 2.1, 3.0 Sep 2021, 3.1 May 2025) rather than a fixed periodicity; left absent per Research.1.md section 4 rather than forcing a number onto a versioned standard.

reports.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/2152 on European business statistics, repealing 10 legal acts in the field of business statistics
reports.description: The EBS Regulation, minted here as the dependency target the EBS manual names as its basic act -- previously unread, per Research.1.md section 12's own flag ('the EBS Regulation (2019/2152) thread... flags as unread', quoted in the scoping doc). Confirmed by direct EUR-Lex fetch this session, independent of the manual's own citation of it.

dependencies.basis: The manual's own text: 'The main tools supporting this work programme are provided by a system of a basic act, the European business statistics (EBS) regulation... Regulation (EU) 2019/2152 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 on European business statistics, repealing 10 legal acts in the field of business statistics (basic act, referred to as the EBS regulation).'
